metaDescription: Selling a mineral interest near Alpine Northwest in Lincoln County, WY? Here's how I run title, check for lease history, and quote it, step by step.
heroLead: I get calls from this stretch of Lincoln County a couple times a year, usually from someone who found a mineral deed while cleaning out a parent's file cabinet and has no idea what to do with it.
intro: The process is the same whether your acreage is one quarter section or a scattered set of fractional interests across several: confirm the legal description, check the county recorder for lease history, then price it against comparable Overthrust Belt transactions. Alpine Northwest sits at the far edge of the play's structural trend, so most of what I find here is undeveloped rather than currently producing.
I'll walk you through each step below in the order I actually do it, not the order a form makes you fill things out.

sections.heading: Step one: confirm what you own
paragraphs: Old deeds up here sometimes describe fractional interests in language that's genuinely confusing, a percentage of a percentage, tied to an original homestead patent from a hundred years back. I match whatever paperwork you have against the Lincoln County plat and current tax roll to nail down the exact acreage and your net mineral share.
This step alone resolves most of the uncertainty people call me with. Once you know precisely what you hold, the rest gets simple.

sections.heading: Step two: check the lease and production history
paragraphs: Next I check whether your tract has ever been under lease, and if so, whether anything was ever drilled. Most Alpine-area sections have old, expired lease filings and no wellbore. That tells me your interest prices as speculative, undeveloped acreage rather than producing minerals.

sections.heading: Step three: price it honestly
paragraphs: I quote against recent comparable trades in Lincoln County, adjusted for your distance from the nearest active unit and whether your tract has ever drawn lease interest. If a number sounds too clean or too high before anyone has looked at your title, be skeptical of it.

faqs.question: How long does the whole process take?
faqs.answer: Title confirmation usually takes a few days once I have your deed information. Closing typically follows within a few weeks.

faqs.question: Do I have to pay anything up front?
faqs.answer: No. I do the title and records work on my end before quoting you.

faqs.question: What if my interest turns out to be very small?
faqs.answer: Small fractional interests still have value and I'll quote them the same way I would a larger tract, just scaled to your actual share.
